info.title: Kestrel API
info.description: Cloud browsers for AI agents. Create a session, then connect any CDP client (Playwright, Puppeteer) to its `connectUrl`. Durations are milliseconds. Errors have one shape; branch on `code` and `retryable`.

CaptchaSolveState.description: `solved` means a token was put into the page (and its callback called, when one was found); the site may still refuse it. `failed`: hand the CAPTCHA to a person.

since.description: When the current, unbroken presence began.

solve.description: Sessions created with `captcha.solve`: the latest solve of a CAPTCHA still present.

SessionCaptcha.description: A CAPTCHA from a known provider is showing on a page. It may already be solved: a solved checkbox stays until the page moves on.

solve.description: Send reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha and Turnstile widgets that show to the deployment's CAPTCHA solver service and put the token into the page. Refused when the deployment has no solver. The page's URL (without query or fragment) and the widget's site key go to that third party, and the page can tell its callback was called by something other than the widget.

server.description: The proxy, as `http://host:port`, `https://host:port` (TLS to the proxy) or `socks5://host:port`.

provider.description: How to ask the proxy for `country`, `region`, `city` and `sticky`. `generic` (the default) sends the username unchanged.

country.description: Exit country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). With a provider adapter, the proxy is asked for it; with `generic`, it only says where your proxy exits, and sets the default `timezone`.

region.description: Exit region or state, in the provider's spelling (e.g. `california`). Needs `country` and a provider adapter that supports it.

city.description: Exit city, in the provider's spelling (e.g. `new york`). Needs `country` and a provider adapter.

sticky.description: Keep the same exit address for requests carrying this id (a sticky session). Needs a provider adapter.

stickyMinutes.description: How long a sticky exit is kept, where the provider lets you choose. Needs `sticky`.

SessionProxy.description: The session's upstream proxy. The username is the one given, before any provider adapter; the password is never returned.

server.description: The proxy, as `http://host:port`, `https://host:port` (TLS to the proxy) or `socks5://host:port`.

username.description: For authentication to the proxy (HTTP Basic, or SOCKS5 username and password).

password.description: Write-only: never stored by the API or returned.

stickyMinutes.description: How long a sticky exit is kept, where the provider lets you choose. Needs `sticky`.

ProxyConfig.description: Send this session's traffic through your own proxy. The proxy resolves hostnames.

Viewport.description: The page's inner size in CSS pixels.

allow.description: If present, only these hostnames may be reached.

persist.description: Save the browser's state back into the profile when the session ends cleanly. Only one session at a time may persist a profile.

idleTimeout.description: End the session after this long with no client attached, in milliseconds.

stopOnDisconnect.description: End the session when its last client disconnects.

recording.description: Record the browser's display to video, retrievable from `/recording` after the session.

timezone.description: The browser's time zone, as pages see it in `Date` and `Intl`. Defaults to the zone of the proxy's exit `country` where that country has one clear zone; otherwise the host's (UTC).

profile.description: Start with a saved profile (`/v1/profiles`). Use the browser's default context: other contexts are not saved.

idleTimeout.description: End the session after this long with no client attached, in milliseconds.

stopOnDisconnect.description: End the session when its last client disconnects.

recording.description: Record the browser's display to video, retrievable from `/recording` after the session.

timezone.description: The browser's time zone, as pages see it in `Date` and `Intl`. Defaults to the zone of the proxy's exit `country` where that country has one clear zone; otherwise the host's (UTC).

profile.description: Start with a saved profile (`/v1/profiles`). Use the browser's default context: other contexts are not saved.

idempotencyKey.description: Repeating a request with the same key returns the original session.

waitForCapacityMs.description: If the platform is full, retry admission for up to this long before answering 503.

egressBytesUp.description: Bytes the browser sent out through the egress gateway (request bodies and tunnelled TLS), counted outside the browser.

egressBytesDown.description: Bytes the browser received through the egress gateway.

connectUrl.description: A wss:// URL (ws:// on a deployment in local mode) for Playwright, Puppeteer or any CDP client. Null unless the session can be connected to.

version.description: The current version. 0 until a session has saved one.

bytes.description: The current version's stored size; 0 if none.

chromeMajor.description: The Chrome major version that saved the current version. Only the same or a newer Chrome opens it.

inUseBy.description: The session that will save the next version (`persist: true`), if one is running.

post.description: Returns when the browser is ready to connect to. `capacity_exhausted` (503) means the platform is full; `quota_exceeded` (429) means the project is over its limit. With `waitForCapacityMs` a full platform is retried before answering.

200.description: An earlier request with the same idempotencyKey: the original session, in its current state.

post.description: Idempotent. Returns at once with the session in `stopping` (or already ended); teardown continues in the background.

post.summary: Mint a token for a running session
post.description: `cdp` re-issues the connect URL. `view` opens live view (frames only) and `control` opens it with mouse and keyboard; both default to 10 minutes and may be up to 1 hour, never past the session's own deadline plus one minute. `singleUse` tokens open one connection and live at most 5 minutes. For `view` and `control`, `url` is a viewer page with the token in the URL fragment; open it in a browser or an iframe-free tab.

get.description: Fragmented MP4 of the browser window, for a session created with `recording: true`. Available while the session runs (up to its latest fragment) and for 24 hours after it ends, from the node it ran on. 404 if the session was not recorded, its node could not record, or the recording has been removed.

post.summary: Screenshot, mouse and keyboard over HTTP
post.description: One action per call on the session's current page, no CDP client needed. Coordinates are CSS pixels of the page (see `width` and `height` in the response). Each call counts as activity for `idleTimeout`. Any action except `screenshot` may set `screenshot: true` to get a PNG of the result.

200.description: A page of events, oldest first.

post.description: An empty profile: saved browser state (cookies, `localStorage` and IndexedDB) that sessions start from with `profile: { id }` and save into with `profile: { id, persist: true }`. `quota_exceeded` past the project's profile limit; `invalid_request` on a deployment without profiles.

delete.description: Removes the profile and its saved state. Sessions already running keep their browser state; a running writer's save is discarded. A second delete is `not_found`.

get.description: The project the API key belongs to, its quotas, and whether the key is an admin key.

get.summary: The project's API keys, newest first
get.description: Revoked keys are included. The keys themselves are never returned.

post.description: The response carries the key once; only a hash is stored. Keys made here are never admin keys.
It stops authenticating at once. Idempotent. A key cannot revoke itself (`conflict`).

get.summary: Sessions and browser time per day
get.description: Whole UTC days ending today. Browser time is counted on the day a session was created.
`not_found` for a key that is not an admin key.

post.summary: Create a project in an organisation (admin keys)
post.description: Names are unique within an organisation (`conflict`).

post.summary: Create an API key in any project (admin keys)
post.description: The key is shown once and is never an admin key.
